messages:
lisa: hitting 400 when calling pdf_tool with document metadata that has a hidden line-separator char (U+2028). stack shows JSON.parse error.

emma: can you paste the request body (redact keys)?

lisa: sure here's payload we send (redacted):
```json
{
  "filename": "report.pdf",
  "metadata": "Author: Alice \\u2028 Version: 1.2",
  "pages": 12
}
```

lisa: server logs -> SyntaxError: JSON.parse: bad control character in string literal at position 45

support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-0921; assigning to eng-oncall

miguel: fyi Chrome's copy/paste can insert U+2028 as literal, and JSON.parse in some runtimes chokes. We should either sanitize input or accept these characters by escaping them server-side.

raj: repro steps worked for me: sending payload with literal \\u2028 in metadata triggers error in Node 14. Code sample to reproduce:
```js
const payload = JSON.stringify({metadata: "line1\\u2028line2"});
JSON.parse(payload); // throws in older engines
```

emma: quick fix for support team: ask customers to run JSON.stringify on their string inputs or replace /\u2028|\u2029/g with "\\u2028". We'll add that to KB.

lisa: did that and customer confirmed it works. Will follow up with a PR that normalizes incoming tool args: replace unescaped U+2028/U+2029 and add clearer 400 message mentioning control characters.

miguel: +1. Also add test case in toolcall parser for these control separators and include a helpful error code e.g., TOOLARGS_400_CONTROL_CHAR.

raj: created branch fix/toolargs-controlchar, adding unit + e2e. I'll link PR when ready.

lisa: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
